page_title: Logging Sucks - Your Logs Are Lying To You

summary.title: Logging Sucks - Your Logs Are Lying To You
summary.one_liner: Traditional string-based logs fail at debugging distributed requests, and emitting one context-rich "wide event" per request with tail sampling fixes this.
takeaways: Logs are optimized for writing, not querying, so string search across services misses context; emit one wide event per request per service instead.
Structured logging is necessary but not sufficient: a useful event needs high-cardinality and high-dimensional fields such as user ID, cart, payment and feature flags.
OpenTelemetry is a delivery protocol; you still must decide what to instrument and add business context yourself.
Use tail sampling: always keep errors, slow requests and key users, and randomly sample the remaining traffic (for example 1-5%).
summary.summary: The article argues that conventional logging (console.log-style text lines, grep and string search) is ill-suited to modern multi-service systems. It proposes the wide event, or canonical log line: a single JSON record per request per service, built up through the request lifecycle with user, cart, payment, error and feature flag context, then emitted once at the end. It includes a TypeScript middleware and handler example, a tail sampling function that keeps errors, slow requests and important users while sampling the rest, and a section on common misconceptions about structured logs, OpenTelemetry, tracing and metrics. The author also promotes an agent skill for implementing these practices.
